facts.text: A xylophone is a musical instrument.
A xylophone is in the percussion family, like instruments you tap or hit.
A xylophone has bars that can play different notes.
The name xylophone means wood sound.
People play a xylophone by tapping the bars with mallets.
A mallet is a kind of stick for playing the xylophone.
Many xylophone bars are made of wood.
Some modern xylophones use synthetic bars instead of wooden bars.
Some xylophones are played with two mallets, one in each hand.
Each xylophone bar is a different length.
Bars with different lengths make different notes when they are tapped.
On many Western xylophones, the bars are arranged like piano keys.
On many Western xylophones, the notes get higher from left to right.
Some xylophones in Africa arrange the bars in a different order.
When a mallet taps a bar, the bar vibrates.
Vibrating things can make sound waves in the air.
Sound waves travel into our ears.
Our eardrums vibrate when sound waves reach them.
A xylophone can play high sounds and low sounds.
A xylophone bar is tuned to a pitch, which means it has its own note.
The xylophone often has a bright, short sound.
A marimba is related to the xylophone and often has a softer sound.
A player can tap one bar, then another bar, to make a simple rhythm.
Xylophones are used in some music classrooms for children's music learning.
Some classroom xylophones are smaller than concert xylophones.
A gentle tap can make a small ting sound for listening and playing.
Xylophones are found in different forms in Africa and Asia.
Some xylophones have tubes or gourds under the bars to help the sound ring.
A Philippine xylophone called a kulintang a kayo has eight tuned slabs on a wooden rack.
A balafon is a West African xylophone-like instrument with wooden keys and gourd resonators.
